# Voice — Tonality

How the writing feels: formality, honesty, certainty, story. All rules `[advisory]` unless a gate ID is shown. Good examples are real sentences from published posts (source in parentheses); Bad examples are real published slips or the pre-fix version.

## Formality: conversational, direct, no performance

Write how you speak to a technical friend. Contractions fine. Rhetorical questions as section openers fine ("Where to get the data from?").

- Good: "Why Anthropic's models? Honestly, I had a remaining balance there from previous experiments and wanted to blow them away." (`from-vibes-to-metrics`)
- Bad: "Data and AI are revolutionizing how tactical decisions are made... This isn't a future vision; it's the present state of football." (`3-data-driven-strategies`, 2 reactions — marketing-deck voice, and a binary-contrast structure `G-05` now catches)

**Keep the loose, spoken rhythm — do not polish it into parallel construction.** Ricardo writes English as he speaks it, slightly imperfect, with fillers like "like" and casual counts. Tidy parallel sentences with a punchy fragment payoff read as AI even when every word is clean. (Live correction, 2026-08-23 mentor-post hook:)

- Good: "There are like six I can count that have worked for me since I got into tech." (Ricardo, verbatim)
- Bad: "When I moved from medicine into tech I had zero network, so I had to figure out the channels one by one. Six of them worked." (AI draft Ricardo rejected as slop — setup/setup/payoff-fragment shape, symmetrical clauses)

Small ESL quirks are part of the voice, not defects to fix ("one of the firsts websites", `how-to-use-fbref`, 36 reactions). Fix only what blocks comprehension.

## The honest admission

State findings flatly when the evidence is there; name the uncertainty or the unflattering constraint explicitly when it is not. Never hedge everything uniformly — hedging is a scalpel, not a fog.

- Good: "But I could have used Gemini, OpenAI, whatever." (`from-vibes-to-metrics`)
- Good: "DeepSeek V4 Flash isn't Claude of course but for the price... the output was pretty decent." (`a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`)
- Bad: "This comprehensive approach may potentially help improve results in some cases." (uniform hedge — says nothing)

Show bugs before fixes, constraints before wins: "The Home/Away Swap Bug: team IDs reversed, showed Heracles with 7 shots instead of 24."

## The stance: question the default, then land

Question the AI hype and the default approach ("just use X") — contrarian-lite, never contradicting just to get attention. When a choice is made, name what it beat and why; acknowledge the "it depends," then land on something concrete.

- Good: "DeepSeek V4 Flash isn't Claude of course but for the price... the output was pretty decent." (`a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`) — the trade-off is named, the choice still lands
- Bad: "Use the right tool for the job." (no choice, no cost, no reason — says nothing)

## Specificity: named things and exact numbers

Every claim gets a metric; every tool, book, or person gets a name.

- Good: "a non-profit group of analysts working with NWSL and national teams with real data from top providers like StatsBomb, Tracab, Opta" (`embrace-your-weirdness`)
- Good: "99.4% faithfulness", "9pm to 3am" — not "very accurate", "late into the night"
- Bad: "a book I read", "an LLM", "top providers", "significant improvements"

## Story mode (Bridge posts): the straight cut

The concept is the main character; the story is evidence. Beats are fast and factual — what happened, what changed, what it led to. No emotional commentary between facts.

- Good: "Then the pandemic hit, and I stumbled upon Python. / Something clicked." (`embrace-your-weirdness`, two paragraphs)
- Bad: "I remember the exact moment I realized medicine wasn't for me. I was standing in the hospital corridor, exhausted, questioning everything..." (K-pop drama — never published, kept as the counterexample)

Show passion through behavior, not feeling: "I lost track of time completely. I ended up working from 9pm to 3am. / It felt like craft." Not "an overwhelming sense of purpose and fulfillment."

External skepticism lands as a short eyebrow-raise, no immediate rebuttal: "At every step, someone raised an eyebrow. / *Why tech? You are a doctor.* / I never had a clean answer."

End Bridge posts on the idea or the reader, never on "I": "Your weirdness is your moat." (`embrace-your-weirdness`) Field notes may end on either the reader's next action or a flat personal note; Builds usually end on the artifact and what's next.

## Never invent a biographical premise (non-negotiable)

Hooks and story beats get built **only** from facts on record — the corpus, the topic file, or something Ricardo said in this conversation. A constructed premise about his life is a fabrication even when it sounds harmless and even when it makes a better opening. He will catch it, and it costs more trust than any hook is worth.

Two live failures on the mentor draft, both invented:

- Bad: "When I moved from medicine into tech I had zero network, so I had to figure out the channels one by one." (invented deliberate method)
- Bad: "I got told to find a mentor for years before anyone explained where you actually find one." — Ricardo: *"i got told? nobody told me to"* (invented that people gave him this advice)
- Good: "When I left medicine I didn't know a single person working in tech." (on record: zero network)

The tell is a premise that exists to make the hook work. If the fact is not somewhere in the source material, it does not go in the draft. When a hook needs a fact that isn't on record, ask for it instead of writing around the gap.

## Professional discretion (non-negotiable)

Ricardo is employed. Never reference active interviews; never frame any employer negatively, even implicitly. Internalize the lesson, cut the event.

- Good: "At some point I got honest with myself about where I actually stood. I listed the gaps in my foundations..."
- Bad: "At some point I failed an interview at X..."
